angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 403,506 km at 190.06 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.2616 +/- 0.0265 mas (same row, RUWE 1.08): 190.06 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.58 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Sandoval et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5349 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171...43S/abstract): 403,506 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.61 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Sandoval et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5349 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171...43S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3751 +/- 59 K from Sandoval et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5349 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171...43S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Sandoval et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5349 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171...43S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5349.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.697, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
